newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL-LOW-SCORING CAVALIERS LOSE ANOTHER, TO HEAT.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL-LOW-SCORING CAVALIERS LOSE ANOTHER, TO HEAT.

text.p: Playing the Cleveland Cavaliers is like a trip to the dentist for other NBA teams. But the dentist is enjoying it even less than the patients.
Alonzo Mourning scored a modest 15 points to lead the Miami Heat to a 71-66 victory over the Cavaliers Saturday in Cleveland's latest low-speed chase.
The Cavs, who have been held to the two lowest totals in franchise history in their last two games, have lost 10 of their last 13 games. They were held to 65 points Wednesday against New York.
"We were terrible," Miami's Tim Hardaway said. "We were just terrible from the get-go. But we got the 'W' and that's all that counts. We missed wide-open shots. I missed some shots I normally make.
"It was like going to the dentist."

P.J. Brown had 12 points and 13 rebounds and Hardaway added 11 points and nine assists for the Atlantic Division-leading Heat, who set a franchise record with their 21st road win of the season. Miami, which won 14 straight road games earlier this season, has just 14 road games left.

"As long as we got more points at the end of the game, that's all that counts," Mourning said. "This ball club has been so successful on the road because we have been able to play in tough situations."
Miami did not allow more than 18 points in any period and scored 24 in the final quarter as it won its third straight game and eighth in the last 10.
"We made enough shots to win it," Miami coach Pat Riley said. "Both sides played good defence. It was a real slow game and we defended their perimeter players very well."
Terrell Brandon scored 15 points and Tyrone Hill and Bobby Phills each added 14 for the Cavaliers, who have been outscored 135-89 over their last six fourth quarters.

In Dallas, Derek Harper had season highs of 29 points and 11 assists and Chris Gatling added 19 points and 12 rebounds as the Mavericks rallied from an 11-point deficit for a 100-97 victory over the Utah Jazz, who had a five-game winning streak snapped.
Dallas won for just the third time in its last 11 games.
Karl Malone scored 36 points to lead Utah, which fell to 11-12 on the road. Malone has averaged 32.7 points in his last six games.
At New Jersey, Grant Hill scored 22 points and had his fourth triple-double of the season as the Detroit Pistons extended their winning streak to five games with a 90-75 victory over the Nets.
Hill added 11 rebounds and 11 assists for the 15th triple of his career and the second in as many weeks.
The Pistons, who have won the last eight meetings with the Nets including three this season, never trailed and led by as many as 16 points in the first half.
Shawn Bradley scored 18 points and Kendall Gill 16 for the Nets, who lost for the 13th time in 17 games.
In Denver, Mitch Richmond had 35 points and a career-high 13 rebounds before fouling out as the Sacramento Kings defeated the Nuggets 113-107.
Kevin Gamble scored 23 points off the bench and former Nugget Mahmoud Abdul-Rauf added 20 points for the Kings, who won for just the seventh time in 16 games.
LaPhonso Ellis scored 27 points and Antonio McDyess and Ricky Pierce each added 23 for Denver.
In Los Angeles, Loy Vaught had 25 points and 13 rebounds as the Clippers overcame Golden State 110-98 despite a 40-point effort by the Warriors' Latrell Sprewell.
Rodney Rogers scored 19 points for the Clippers, who won for the fourth time in five games.
Sprewell registered his third 40-point performance this season. He hit 12-of-22 shots from the field, including five three-pointers, and made 11-of-12 free throw attempts.
The Warriors lost for the fifth time in six games.
In Milwaukee, Don MacLean scored seven of his season-high 29 points in the final three minutes, sparking the Philadelphia 76ers to a 109-100 victory over the slumping Bucks.
Rookie Allen Iverson had 23 points and a season-high 14 assists and Jerry Stackhouse added 21 points for the 76ers, who are 3-3 since a 13-game losing streak.
Vin Baker had 22 points and 10 rebounds before fouling out for the Bucks, who have lost 13 of their last 19 games.
In Toronto, Walt Williams scored 33 points as the Raptors cruised to a 110-86 win over the Phoenix Suns, who dropped their sixth straight game.

Rookie Marcus Camby and Doug Christie scored 17 points apiece for the Raptors, who had lost four of their last five games. Toronto allowed just nine points in the fourth quarter in its first win ever against Phoenix.
Wesley Person scored 23 points for the Suns, who fell to 4-21 on the road.
